item.title: Flanders 0.18.4
item.description:
### Added
- **Filter the sidebar with ⌘F.** Press ⌘F while the connection tree is active
  to reveal a filter box under the sidebar header. Type to narrow the list of
  databases — connections always stay visible — and press Esc to clear the
  filter, then again to dismiss it. ⌘F still works as normal inside the SQL
  editor and other text fields.

item.title: Flanders 0.18.3
item.description:
### Improved
- **Binary columns are now readable.** BINARY, VARBINARY, BLOB, BIT and spatial
  columns show a tidy placeholder such as `[varbinary]` instead of raw bytes, so
  a row of hashes or images no longer fills the grid with noise. The underlying
  value is untouched, so editing and primary-key matching keep working.
- **A finessed Navicat import panel.** The From Navicat window has been rebuilt
  around a live status card, a fixed footer whose Close button is always
  available, and a Stop button that halts a whole-drive search the instant you
  press it. Results stream in as they are found, with a running count and timer.

item.title: Flanders 0.18.2
item.description:
### Improved
- **The Navicat backup search now shows what it's doing, live.** As it looks it
  tells you which location it's scanning, streams each backup into the list the
  moment it's found, and shows a running count and timer. A whole-drive search
  can be stopped at any time.

item.title: Flanders 0.18.1
item.description:
### Added
- **Search for Navicat backups anywhere.** The Navicat import window now has a
  Search button that looks in the obvious places (Navicat's folder plus
  Documents, Desktop and Downloads), with a “Whole drive” option to search your
  home folder and mounted volumes too — handy if your backups have been moved.

item.title: Flanders 0.18.0
item.description:
### Added
- **Import backups straight from Navicat.** The Backup view has a new
  “From Navicat” button that finds the Navicat backups on your Mac for the
  current database and imports them into Flanders in one click — a simple way
  to bring your history across when you switch. Navicat's `.nb3` backups are
  reconstructed faithfully (every table and row, binary data included), and you
  can also browse to a `.nb3` file yourself.

item.title: Flanders 0.17.13
item.description:
### Fixed
- **Restoring backups with binary data no longer corrupts it.** Dumps that
  contain binary columns (for example WordPress/Wordfence tables keyed on a
  binary hash) are now restored byte-for-byte via the MySQL client when
  available, so values like binary primary keys come back exactly as they were.
  Plain text backups continue to use the fast built-in restore with full
  progress. Restore is also disabled until you're connected to a server.

item.title: Flanders 0.17.12
item.description:
### Fixed
- The About window's GitHub button now opens the public releases page.

item.title: Flanders 0.17.11
item.description:
### Added
- **Choose whether a restore drops existing tables.** The restore confirmation
  now has a “Drop existing tables first” switch. Leave it on (the default) to
  replace the data cleanly; turn it off to run the backup as-is and merge into
  what's already there. The dialog explains the effect of each choice.

item.title: Flanders 0.17.10
item.description:
### Fixed
- **Restore is now reliable for standard mysqldump files.** Two issues are
  resolved: statements preceded by a comment line (as mysqldump writes them) are
  no longer skipped during restore, and every table the backup defines is now
  cleared before restoring regardless of the dump's contents. Restoring a
  WordPress or other mysqldump backup now replaces the data cleanly instead of
  reporting "table already exists" and duplicate-key errors.

item.title: Flanders 0.17.9
item.description:
### Improved
- **The backup log is now selectable, with Copy and Clear buttons.** Select any
  part of the restore/backup log to copy it, or use the Copy button to grab the
  whole log at once — handy for keeping a record or sharing what happened.

item.title: Flanders 0.17.8
item.description:
### Fixed
- **Restore now always replaces, so it can't duplicate your data.** Backups made
  by other tools (for example a mysqldump without drop-table statements) used to
  be layered on top of the existing rows during a restore, duplicating
  everything. Flanders now clears each table the backup defines before restoring
  it, with foreign-key checks handled automatically — the restore replaces the
  data cleanly, exactly as the confirmation describes.

item.title: Flanders 0.17.7
item.description:
### Added
- **The backup details pane now appears in the sidebar's Backups list too**, not
  only the Backup tool — select any backup to see its full contents wherever you
  are.

### Notes
- Flanders is free to use throughout the beta (every 0.x release). A licence
  will only be needed from version 1.0 onward; nothing you're using today will
  stop working.

item.title: Flanders 0.17.6
item.description:
### Added
- **Backup details pane.** Select any backup to open a details panel on the
  right showing everything about it: database, connection, when it was made,
  full or structure-only, size on disk and uncompressed, table and row counts,
  character set and originating server version where available, the list of
  tables inside the file, and the dump's header. Reveal and Verify are one
  click away.

item.title: Flanders 0.17.5
item.description:
### Improved
- **Importing backups now handles dumps of any character set.** Dropping a
  `.sql` or `.sql.gz` file made by mysqldump (or another tool) no longer fails
  when the dump contains non-UTF-8 data — a very common case. The file is
  imported and remains fully restorable.
- **Drop a backup anywhere in the Backup view to import it**, not only onto the
  Backups folder in the sidebar. The panel highlights as you drag a file over
  it.

item.title: Flanders 0.17.4
item.description:
### Added
- **Links to getflanders.com in the app** — Flanders ▸ Flanders Website, and a
  Help menu with Website / Features / What's New.

item.title: Flanders 0.17.3
item.description:
### Changed
- Licence agreement and app copyright corrected to name Whitewater Training
  Limited as the author (the agreement is shown once more on update).

item.title: Flanders 0.17.2
item.description:
### Added
- **Drag & drop backup import.** Drop a `.sql` or `.sql.gz` dump from Finder
  onto a database's *Backups* folder in the sidebar: Flanders copies it into
  its managed backups (the original stays put), scans it for table/row counts
  and gzip integrity, and it's immediately available to Restore like any
  other backup. Imported records are marked with the source filename.

### Fixed
- Backup verification no longer flags imported third-party dumps for missing
  `DROP TABLE` statements (that check now applies only to Flanders-authored
  dumps).

item.title: Flanders 0.17.1
item.description:
### Added
- **First-launch licence agreement.** Flanders now requires acceptance of an
  End User Licence Agreement before first use (England & Wales law): use at
  your own discretion, software provided as-is and may be withdrawn without
  notice, intended for non-production environments, and users are responsible
  for their own independent, tested backups. Acceptance is version-stamped, so
  materially changed terms are shown again.

item.title: Flanders 0.17.0
item.description:
### Added
- **Sparkle auto-updates.** Flanders now checks for updates daily and via
  Flanders ▸ Check for Updates…. Updates are EdDSA-signed and served from the
  public `ijasonwhite/flanders-updates` repo (appcast + notarized zips only —
  no source). `scripts/release.sh` signs, uploads and publishes the appcast
  entry automatically after notarization.
- **Licensing scaffold (dark).** Offline-verifiable Ed25519 licence keys
  (Stripe Checkout webhook → signed key by email → paste into Settings ▸
  Licence, verified with CryptoKit, stored in the Keychain). Nothing is gated
  yet — plumbing only, ahead of a pricing decision. Server side is vanilla
  PHP in `licensing/`.
